BiblicalUsage: Delilah is the Philistine woman who loved Samson and sold him, and her name is the story of the fall of the strongest man in Israel. She pressed him daily with her words until his soul was vexed unto death, and he told her the secret of his strength. The Philistines bound him, put out his eyes, and made him grind in the prison house.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Delilah is the warning about the slow press: she did not conquer Samson in a day, she wore him down word by word, and the strongest man fell to the smallest weapon. My position is plain: the secret of our strength is the Lord, and it must never be given away to please another.
